shell.title: Meet Amanda Hecimovic
shell.description: Learn about my approach, credentials, and values that guide my practice.

sections.title: A steady place to make sense of what you are carrying
paragraphs: Hi, I’m Amanda (she/her), and I’m a **Registered Clinical Counsellor** (license #29097) with the [BC Association of Clinical Counsellors](https://bcacc.ca/about-us/).

While my counselling work currently focuses on eating disorder recovery and disordered eating, I also welcome clients who may be looking for support with anxiety, depression, life transitions, self-worth, and burnout.

Early on in my undergraduate degree, I had the pleasure of meeting people in eating disorder recovery. They shared their stories with me, describing the isolation and stigma they felt and the lack of resources available to help them in their recovery.

Hearing their stories and witnessing their resilience and vulnerability inspired me to volunteer with a local non-profit, [**Looking Glass Foundation**](https://www.lookingglassbc.com/), to help increase access to mental health support for those in eating disorder recovery. I deeply cherished my time there, so I returned as a practicum student during my graduate program to deepen my skill set.

I am truly passionate about this work. I have seen people make incredible strides in their recovery, from their eating disorder completely ruling their lives to thriving and leading lives aligned with who they are at their core, not the eating disorder. They have shown me and others that **recovery is possible**.

When I'm not counselling, you'll find me helping youth with learning differences develop their literacy skills, discovering new music, attending concerts, going for long walks by the ocean, connecting (and usually laughing) with loved ones, and improving my watercolour skills.

sections.title: My Approach
paragraphs: Because I believe that no two healing journeys are the same, I meet clients where they are and honour their individual pace, needs, and capacity throughout the counselling process. I strive to meet each person with warmth, empathy, non-judgement, and a desire to truly understand their unique experiences.
Clients have shared that they also apprecaited these qualities when working with me:

- **Authenticity**: I try to be the same person in sessions as I am outside of sessions. I won't be a blank-slate - I might swear, smile/laugh/shed a tear with you, or make a dated pop cultural reference that makes it glaringly obvious that I'm a millenial. 
- **Playfulness & Humour** - When the timing feels right, I will likely crack a joke when it feels therapeutically relevant. Dark, witty, quirky humour is welcome here.
- **Accountablility** - Counselling can be hard work, and our systems may try to protect us from the discomfort in different ways, like turning to or increasing the frequency of old coping strategies that may not be helpful. Although it can feel uncomfortable to confront, I may gently challenge you or direct your attention to the ways you may be getting in your own way, helping you stay accountable to your goals and values.

Through my own experience as a counselling client, I know how important it is to find a counsellor who feels like **the right fit for you**, where you feel safe, respected, and supported. With the right match, you can truly transform your life.

sections.title: Modalities
paragraphs: My work is integrative, blending mind-body therapeutic approaches with a particular focus on how our early experiences impact our development and may continue to effect our mental wellness in adulthood. Together, we can explore the approaches and strategies that feel most supportive and aligned for you, tailoring counselling to your unique needs.

The therapeutic approaches I typically draw from include:

- [Accelerated Experiential Dynamic Psychotherapy (AEDP)](https://aedpinstitute.org/about-aedp-psychotherapy/)
- [Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)](https://www.psychologytoday.com/ca/therapy-types/acceptance-and-commitment-therapy)
- [Compassion-Focused Therapy](https://www.aptcanada.com/compassion-focused-therapy.html)
- [Internal Family Systems (IFS)](https://ifs-institute.com/)
- [Motivational Interviewing](https://www.psychologytoday.com/ca/therapy-types/motivational-interviewing)
- [Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT)](https://beckinstitute.org/about/understanding-cbt/)
- Mindfulness
- Psychodynamic approaches

sections.title: How we work together
sections.description: Counselling here is collaborative and practical, honouring your lived experience, knowledge, and wisdom throughout the process

items.title: Collaborative care
items.description: While I can help guide you, I am not an expert on your life and what works best for you. You know yourself best, which is why counselling tends to work beter when the goals, pace, and focus are shaped together. In sessions, I may encourage you to let me know what works and what doesn't, so we can make our work together feel as effective as possible

items.title: Respect for lived experience
items.description: We've all lived through experiences that have shaped our identities, beliefs, relationships, behaviours, and needs. And many of us have experiences with systems in society that have caused immeasurable harm. I'm dedicated to my continued learning and unlearning to support folks who have been impacted by these systems.

items.title: Practical support
items.description: What's practical for one person may not feel practical for another. Whether you're someone who wants to work towards tangible goals, create a dedicated space for self-reflection, or practice new skills, we can use sessions to focus on what you would find most helpful for you in your daily life
